builds.title: Japanese — Aggro Mass Yumi
builds.description:
Beginner version: keep making villagers at your Town Center throughout the game. New villagers should gather food unless a step says otherwise.

Start with 2 villagers gathering food, 2 chopping wood and 2 building. Food means sheep, berries or farms. Gold means the gold mine beside your base. A Spearman is made at the Barracks; Yumi archers are made at an Archery Range.

Follow the instructions in order. Times are rough guides, not deadlines: wait until you have the resources. Skip the optional tower steps while learning. Keep training Yumi, make Spearmen against horse units, and avoid attacking underneath the enemy Town Center.

Castle Age is the next stage after Feudal Age. Move to it after dealing damage or when you need stronger units. In Castle, keep archers behind Mounted Samurai. Put the first Yorishiro from Floating Gate into the Archery Range to speed up its upgrade; collect relics with monks when safe.

Matchups: against English or House of Lancaster, their villagers can shoot your spears; adapt or skip the early attack. Against Ottoman, French or Jeanne d’Arc, keep Spearmen ready for horse units. If the enemy has a large horse army, retreat, protect your villagers and save for Castle.

Based on the linked video transcript.
builds.author: Spoonman

steps.description: Use 1 villager to build a Barracks and 1 to build a Farmhouse beside berries.
Send both builders to food when finished. Keep 2 villagers on wood. Send new villagers to food.
Train 1 Spearman at the Barracks. Send him towards the enemy gold mine.
Train 2 more Spearmen. You now have 3. Stop making them for now.
Use your 3 Spearmen to attack enemy gold miners. Stay away from the enemy Town Center.
Keep chopping until you can build a Forge and have paid for your 3 Spearmen.
Build a Forge beside your gold. Send 3 villagers to mine gold. Keep everyone else on food.
For your first games, skip the optional enemy-base tower. Continue saving for the next age.
At 400 food and 200 gold, advance to Feudal Age. Choose Kura Storehouse; use 3–4 builders.
While Kura is building, put 10 villagers on wood, 2–3 on gold, and everyone else on food.
Once Feudal Age finishes, build 1 Archery Range. Keep training Yumi archers there.
Research Double Broadaxe at a Lumber Camp and Tawara at a Farmhouse when affordable.
Build a 2nd Archery Range. Keep training Yumi archers from both ranges.
Research the Spearman upgrade at your Barracks. Make extra Spearmen if the enemy has horse units.
Keep 12–13 villagers on wood and 2–3 on gold. Send all other villagers to food.
When Kura creates a farm, send 1 food villager to work it. Build houses before reaching your population limit.
If you skipped the tower, skip this step too. Tower upgrades are an optional advanced choice.
Send Yumi and Spearmen together to attack exposed enemy villagers. Pull back if their army is stronger.
Build a 3rd Archery Range when you can afford it and keep your existing ranges training units.
At the Forge, research +1 ranged attack and +1 ranged armor. Research Takezaiku at a Farmhouse.
Select your Town Center and buy the Daimyo Manor upgrade when you have enough stone.
Train 1 Yumi Bannerman at an Archery Range. Keep him near your Yumi to improve their damage.
With Yumi: shoot, move away, then shoot again. Use Spearmen to protect them from horse units.
Aim for 30–40 Yumi. Attack enemy villagers gathering food or gold outside their Town Center.
Use your Scout to check the enemy. If they have few soldiers, attack; if they have more, retreat.
When ready for Castle Age, move wood villagers to gold. Example: 18 food, 12 gold, 3 wood.
Save 1200 food and 600 gold. Advance to Castle Age with Floating Gate. Protect villagers while it builds.
Upgrade Yumi at your range. Build a Stable and train Mounted Samurai to fight in front of your archers.
